city.caveat: This is the official city record as kept, without adjustments. It joins several observing sites over the years, and a move, a new instrument or the city growing around a station can shift readings (city growth mostly warms nights); NOAA's adjusted climate datasets correct for these. Treat any single number as approximate.

text.lede: Yesterday's high of 56°F was typical for November 13.
text.p_yest: The high of 56°F was typical for November 13. The normal high for the date is 61°F, and the record is 80°F (1902, 1945). The low of 48°F was typical for November 13.
text.t_rec: Record highs keep coming. Record lows have nearly stopped.
text.p_rec: If Norfolk's climate weren't changing, every year would have the same chance of holding a daily record. Since 2000, Norfolk has set 17 standing record lows, far fewer than the 64 that chance alone would give, and 103 record highs, far more than the 64 that chance alone would give. The 2010s hold the most record highs of any decade (45). Norfolk's all-time high is 105°F, on August 7, 1918.
text.t_chg: Norfolk has warmed, days and nights alike
text.p_chg: Across 152 complete years: Norfolk's average low has risen +0.10°F per decade (95% range +0.05 to +0.15), about +1.5°F since 1874. Norfolk's average high has risen +0.17°F per decade (95% range +0.13 to +0.22), about +2.6°F since 1874.
text.t_mon: Lows rose in 7 of 12 months. Highs rose in 9 of 12 months.
text.t_rain: Rain and snow: no clear long-term change
text.p_rain: Norfolk's yearly precipitation shows no clear long-term change (+0.11 inches per decade, a range that includes zero). The 1991–2020 normal is 49.1 inches a year. The wettest year was 1889 (70.72 in); the driest, 1986 (26.48 in).
